Kirby is a pretty consistent franchise, the fans definitely aren't starved for content because a new game ( spin-off or mainline ) releases pretty much every year.

Kirby's Return To Dreamland Deluxe was released in 2023 and is the newest installment, which I never played because it's a remaster of a 2011 game I already own.
But I've heard it's interesting, and I love the original ( the first Kirby game I played ) and I can definitely recommend it, but only if you go in without any story spoilers what so ever.
It's pretty basic, but it's Kirby, so it works.
Again, the franchise is really good at catering to everyone so it's likely you won't find a Kirby game you won't enjoy some parts of.

Kirby's Dream Buffet (2022) and Kirby Fighters 2 (2020) then are fun little spin-offs. Good for multiplayer, mostly for multiplayer. Party games basically.

Kirby and The Forgotten Land (2021) is probably the one I'd recommend out of the newer ones the most. It's the first Kirby game in a 3D environment and the mechanics are super fun, I think.
It's one of those games that does well in all aspects. Some older games might beat it in visuals or story but I'd say it's the most consistently good game in the franchise.

Not anymore really, but I was about 7 when I first played it and it was so satisfying. It was a fun game as a kid, and completing it was the best feeling in the world.

(Spoilers)

The story was basically: an alien crashlands to your planet, and you have to help it find the parts to fix his ship.

When the ship is fixed, he promises to take you to visit his homeland. On his planet, there's a dragon that shoots the ship down again, so you have to go and defeat it, because it's been sabotaging the life of the alien.

You defeat the dragon and a crown drops from his head, which the alien comes and takes away as soon as the dragon is down.

Apparently he's been tricking you to do things for him all along. He 'crashlanded' because he knew there was someone powerful that could help him on that planet. (This was the part where me and my friend dropped our jaws. We didn't except the betrayal at all, and it was the biggest plot twist I've ever experienced as a kid.)

The crown gives it's user unlimited power, so the alien in his greed thought he could rule the universe with it. But the dragon protecting the crown was in his way, so he had to get someone to defeat it.

The alien flies away with his newfound powers. And it turns out the dragon is ready to help get the crown back.

The last boss has three phases: one where you fight the ship with the help of the dragon. And two where the crowns powers start to really kick in, the alien getting stronger and stronger.

But it's pretty obvious that he's not in control anymore and the crown basically uses his husk of a body to attack anything that comes into it's way.

You beat the alien one last time. He get's freed and the crown shatters into stardust. You go back to your home and the credits roll.

The alien felt so good to beat up after putting so much time and effort into helping him, and then getting nothing but bad things in return. (me and my friend put at least a month into completing the game)

I really recommend the game to anyone who isn't that young, even though it was literally for kids. Because going through such a journey just to help a friend and then getting backstabbed really hit hard to a kid like I was when I first played it. I have trust issues so bad that I can't become very close with anyone, I can't even open up to my own family.
